headline: Hot PPI and a sixth PBOC drain stall the rally; 10Y CCDC flat at 1.587% near record lows
summary: CGBs consolidated after last week's 6bp rally. The CCDC 10-year edged up 0.1bp to 1.587% and the 30-year 0.1bp to 2.028%, while futures slipped (TL −0.14%, T −0.06%) and the on-the-run 260016 held near 1.57%. The belly was mixed: the 5-year fell 0.6bp to 1.305%, a fresh 1-year low, but the 7-year rose 1.0bp, and the 2-year was unchanged at 1.216%. Policy banks tracked CGBs at 10Y and the long end (CDB 10-year flat at about 1.636%, spread unchanged at 4.9bp; ADBC and EXIM 10-year +0.1bp), but lagged at 3–5Y, where CDB 5-year rose 0.8bp and its spread widened 1.4bp to 11.5bp.
drivers: Factory prices jump, consumer prices cool

October PPI rose 5.7% y/y (forecast 5.3%, prior 5.0%), the fastest since June 2022, driven by oil, coal and gas, while CPI slowed to 0.7% (forecast 0.8%) and core CPI to 0.8% from 1.0%. Bonds read it as cost-push rather than demand, so they only saw mild profit-taking at the long end after record-low yields.
PBOC keeps draining, funding edges up

The PBOC ran RMB182bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB226bn maturing, a sixth straight net drain (RMB44bn), and overnight Shibor rose 3.1bp to 1.314% and 7-day 1.5bp to 1.361%. Funding holding above the 1.25% anchor kept the 2-year flat and capped the front end.

The Shanghai Composite rose 0.32% to 3,661 on banks and coal while ChiNext fell 0.27% and turnover dropped about RMB175bn to RMB1.48tn, so the haven bid behind Friday's rally faded. The PBOC fixed the yuan at 6.7188, its weakest since Oct 22, and the State Council pledged on Nov 6 to strengthen mechanisms that stabilise the stock market.

ADBC's 3-year tap cleared at 1.2155% with 5.6 times cover and its 10-year at 1.6110% with 6.6 times. Government bond net issuance has reached about 83% of the annual plan versus 87% a year ago, with only two 30-year CGB reopenings left (Nov 20 and Dec 2), which supports the long end into year-end.

Energy-driven cost push that squeezes margins rather than signalling demand; bonds looked through it.

A tidy-up, not tightening: the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.56–1.62% CCDC range. The hot PPI is energy cost-push while CPI and core inflation are cooling, the 1.25% overnight anchor is priced as a de facto cut and year-end supply is light, so the trend stays lower; but the 10-year is at a 1-year low, 2s10s is at a 1-year low of 37bp, the PBOC is draining daily and shrank its 3-month outright repos to slow the rally, so I would buy dips rather than chase. I keep the 10-year buy level at 1.61–1.62%, the 5Y-into-10Y switch, an underweight in policy banks against CGBs at 10Y and the long end, and a preference for ADBC/EXIM over CDB. Strong October trade or credit data (due this week) or a sustained equity rebound would push the 10-year back toward 1.62%, while weak credit and activity data could take it to 1.56%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year was unchanged at 1.216%, at its 1-year low (1st percentile, average 1.306%), and the 1-year slipped 0.2bp to 1.167%. Overnight Shibor rose 3.1bp to 1.314% as the PBOC drained for a sixth day, so funding sits above the 1.25% anchor and the front end has little room left.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: 2s5s10s fell 1.3bp to −19.3bp, a new 1-year rich extreme (0th percentile, average −7.8bp), as the 5-year dropped 0.6bp to 1.305% while the 10-year edged up. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp steepened 0.7bp to 28.2bp, still 0.8bp in the money and inside the 31bp stop; the 7-year cheapened 1bp, lifting 5s7s10s to −7.4bp (11th percentile).
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year rose 0.1bp to 1.587%, just above Friday's 1-year low, so the 1.61–1.62% buy level was not reached. Against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −24.9bp, about the 81st percentile against a −29.4bp average.
buckets.call: Buy 10-year CGBs on a back-up to 1.61–1.62%, target 1.57%, stop 1.645%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year rose 0.1bp to 2.028% and 10s30s is flat at 44.1bp, about the 32nd percentile against a 45.8bp average. The 50-year fell 0.8bp to 2.144%, squeezing 30s50s to 11.6bp (6th percentile); only two 30-year reopenings remain this year, which supports the block but leaves little spread cushion.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is unchanged at 4.9bp over CGB (16th percentile, average 9.8bp), so the switch from ~3bp is still about 2bp in the money. CDB 5-year widened 1.4bp to 11.5bp (18th percentile) as policy banks lagged at 3–5Y, while the 2-year spread of 11.7bp stays at its 1-year tight.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.4bp more than CDB (77th percentile, average 1.3bp) and EXIM 2.4bp (64th percentile, average 2.0bp). The pickup reflects heavy tap supply rather than credit, and demand is strong: ADBC's 10-year tap drew 6.6 times cover at 1.611%.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, at its 1-year low (3rd percentile, average 10.5bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also at its 1-year tight (average 12.6bp). Long policy bank bonds were unchanged today and keep moving one for one with CGBs, leaving no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

watch: Next: October trade data (Tue Nov 10), US CPI (Nov 10, US time), October credit data around Nov 10–15, savings bond sales Nov 10–19, daily PBOC overnight operations at 1.25%, the FX RRR hike taking effect on Nov 15, October activity data in mid-November, and the LPR and a 30-year CGB reopening on Nov 20.
